elements.content: Communication Goal: I can say and use numbers 1–12.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: MODULE 1. FIRST CONTACT & PERSONAL IDENTITY
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Numbers 1–12
- Materials: vocabulary cards, audio, reading handout
Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.
Recycles numbers 0–20 from Lesson 1.6.
Recycled language: one, two, three.
Answer from memory: which word belongs to this topic?
Which word belongs to this topic?
Core Active Vocabulary (12 items):

one — the number 1. Example: I have one brother.
two — the number 2. Example: Two students are absent.
three — the number 3. Example: There are three chairs.
four — the number 4. Example: There are four tables.
five — the number 5. Example: I have five books.
six — the number 6. Example: Six students are here.
seven — the number 7. Example: There are seven days in a week.
eight — the number 8. Example: Eight chairs are free.
nine — the number 9. Example: Nine people work here.
ten — the number 10. Example: Ten euros, please.
eleven — the number 11. Example: There are eleven chairs.
twelve — the number 12. Example: Twelve months make a year.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• How many ... are there?
• There are twelve.
• I have two ...
• Count from one to twelve.
• It is number seven.
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'the number 1'?
Which word means 'the number 2'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Say the v in five and seven clearly.
FIVE, SEVEN, ELEVEN, TWELVE.
Listen and repeat three times.
Which word carries the main stress?
Grammar focus: Numbers 1–12.
Numbers 1–12 are irregular and must be learnt. Use a plural noun after numbers above one: two books, twelve chairs.
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.
Choose the correct word for 7.
Choose the correct sentence.
Complete the sentence.
Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
There are twelve students in the class. Six are girls and six are boys. There are four tables and eight chairs.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: How many chairs are there? B: There are eleven. A: And how many tables? B: Three.
Speaking: Pair and group tasks: Count objects, say phone numbers and prices using numbers 1–12.

• How many ... are there?
• There are twelve.
• I have two ...
Writing: Write four to five sentences about "Ge A1 Numbers 1 12" using the target grammar.
